questions.q: What is the first diagnostic question to ask when a user reports an access problem?
options: What is the user's job title?
Can they reach the page or control at all, or can they reach it but something about the data looks wrong?
How long has the user worked at the company?
What browser is the user using?
questions.explain: This question immediately splits the problem into the function security path or the data security path, which require different troubleshooting steps.

questions.q: In the function security troubleshooting path, what should be checked after confirming the expected role was provisioned?
options: The user's data access set value
Whether the underlying data exists at all
The company's chart of accounts
Whether Simulate Navigator confirms the role includes the menu item or button in question
questions.explain: Simulate Navigator is the next step for confirming whether the provisioned role actually includes the function being tested.

questions.q: In the data security troubleshooting path, what is identified as the single most common root cause?
options: A blank or wrong security context value
A corrupted user password
The user's job title being misspelled
An outdated web browser
questions.explain: A blank or incorrect security context value (such as a missing business unit or data access set) is called out as the most common cause of data security issues.

questions.q: Why is 'adding a broader job role to make an access complaint go away, without confirming the specific gap' considered a trap?
options: It is always the fastest and safest fix
It has no real downside in Oracle Fusion
It is how segregation-of-duties conflicts get quietly created, since it grants more access than the actual gap required
It is required by Oracle's support policy
questions.explain: Over-provisioning as a quick fix risks creating unintended SoD conflicts by granting broader access than what was actually missing.

questions.q: Sometimes an access complaint turns out not to be a security problem at all. What is an example given of this?
options: The user's password expired
There is simply no data yet in the business unit being checked, which can look identical to a data security failure
The user's job role was deleted
The ledger does not support multiple currencies
questions.explain: A lack of data in the relevant scope can present exactly like a data security failure, even though there is no actual access problem — a setup gap, not a security gap.
